description:
FOUND BY THE MERGE-TIME SWEEP of the s470bq batch (the first full sweep the
batch ever had): the run reported its only NEW SHORTFALL, `perl-tests/eval.t
9 -> 10 planned row(s) NEVER PRODUCED`, and it survived the serial re-run, so
it was not load noise.

THE ROW: eval.t test 6.

    print eval '$foo = /';   # this tests for a call through fatal()
    like($@, qr/Search/);

perl 5.40.3, probed:  ret=undef, $@ = "Search pattern not terminated at
(eval 1) line 1."

PCL at d59e58c (the base):  the eval DIED, but with a leaked CL host error
("The value nil is not of type real at (eval 3) line 1.") -> `not ok 6`.

PCL with the s470bq flag-day:  ret=1, $@ = "".  The eval SUCCEEDED.

THE MECHANISM.  `Pl::ExprToCL::_parse_regex_content` finds the closing
delimiter with `rindex`, which for an UNTERMINATED literal lands on the
OPENING delimiter (or on nothing).  For the two-character content `/` + "\n"
that gives $end_pos == $prefix_len, and the arithmetic below then reads an
EMPTY pattern with the newline as the FLAGS.  An empty pattern matches, so the
statement evaluated to 1.

The function is PRE-EXISTING and byte-identical to the base; what changed is
that the s470bq keyword form makes its output the EMITTED `:pat`/`:flags`,
where before only the interpolation gate consumed it and the raw string went
to `p-regex` for the runtime to re-parse.  A latent bug became observable â
and became a SILENT WRONG, which is worse than the leaked CL error it
replaced: an invalid program that used to die now produces a value.

THE FIX (one line + its comment): rule 12 â the missing case says so.

    die "Search pattern not terminated\n" if $end_pos <= $prefix_len;

perl's own text, because it is free here and it is the accurate diagnosis.
The die reaches the statement-level machinery, so inside a string eval it
becomes a trappable $@ (the #363 shape) and at file level it is an announced
drop, never silence.

MEASURED.
* `eval '$foo = /'` -> ret=undef, $@ =~ /Search/ â perl's answer; test 6 now
  PASSES where the base had `not ok 6`.
* corpus-diff vs the pre-fix commit: emission IDENTICAL across 111 files + 6
  shapes; silent drops 5, unchanged.  No generation bump (nothing moved).
* full sweep: GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, drops 5 = census,
  SHORTFALL back to baseline (+0), TOTAL passing 18644 -> 18645 (+1).
  `baselines/pass-baseline.tsv` eval.t PARTIAL 128/32 -> 129/31, edited ROW
  BY ROW with the cause; test 6 was never a blessed fail row, so
  `fail-baseline.tsv` is untouched.
* gate 211 files / 7206 tests, green except the 13 standing pclxs xs rows.

GUARD: `Pl/t/ir-data-form-01.t` rows 57-58, INVERSE-VERIFIED (row 57 fails
with the die removed, row 58 passes either way â so the guard is proved not to
have widened into the valid population).  Row 58 is the negative half: six
terminated delimiter spellings (`/b/`, `m{c}`, `//`, `qr/a/i`, `m!b!g`,
`qr {b}`), all probed against perl 5.40.3, all unchanged.

=== DONE (s470bq-merge) ===
Shipped with the batch.  The lesson worth keeping: a parse that MOVES from a
consumer to the emitter must be re-read for rule 12 at the move, because a
tolerant parse behind a runtime that re-did the work becomes an authoritative
one that invents a value.
title: An unterminated regex literal must DIE (rule 12) â the compile-time pattern/flags split had no missing-case arm
